blocks.text: 🏦Story Returns: Bamu and the Bank Years passed. Bamu’s farm expanded. His harvest improved. His savings grew. He trusted the bank the way a child trusts a roof over his head. Until one morning. Bank Teller: “Your account is temporarily unavailable.” Bamu: “But it’s my money.” Bank Teller: “It’s under review.” Temporary stretched into days. Days into silence. Bamu went home without answers. That silence taught him something no book ever had.

items.meaning: A system where another party holds and controls your assets for you.
When a centralized authority restricts access to your funds.
When you believe you own something, but control belongs to someone else.

blocks.prompt: If your entire life savings depended on someone else’s decision…

blocks.text: would you still call it ownership?

🧒Story Returns: The Curious Child The child from the village was older now. Regina held a phone the way previous generations held books. Her teacher drew a door on the board. Teacher: “This door opens with a key.” Regina: “Who keeps the key?” Teacher: “You do. And only you.” That day, Regina learned a word that would follow her for life: Self‑custody.

items.meaning: Holding and controlling your own assets without intermediaries.

History leaves patterns. Every system that controls value eventually tightens control. Banks. Payment apps. Governments. As value grows: surveillance increases freezes increase exclusions increase Self‑custody appears as an exit, not a rebellion. 📊Analysis Summary Custodial failures spike during crises Compliance grows faster than user protection Individuals seek sovereignty Wallet adoption follows instability.

In the coming decade: wallets will replace bank accounts keys will replace identity documents self‑custody will be taught like literacy Those who learn early will move calmly.
